title: The Ghosts of Five Supernovas
explanation:
# Rewritten for General Audience

After painstaking observations spanning 200 hours through a Moroccan telescope, astronomers captured the colorful remnants of five stellar explosions scattered across a patch of sky as wide as a thousand full moons—delicate red and blue filaments of hydrogen and oxygen gas still expanding outward from explosions that occurred thousands of years ago. Early humans may have glimpsed these ancient supernovas as brilliant new stars blazing in the constellation Auriga before fading away over weeks or months, leaving behind these ghostly, glowing shells of shocked gas that still illuminate the night sky today.
